description:
The Motorisation of Traditional Crafts scheme was launched by the Government of India in 2019. 

This initiative aims to enhance the productivity and efficiency of traditional crafts by introducing motorized tools and machinery. 

The scheme is part of a broader effort to modernize traditional industries and improve the livelihoods of artisans and craftsmen across the country. 

The primary objective of the Motorisation of Traditional Crafts scheme is to increase the income of artisans by reducing the time and effort required to produce traditional crafts. 

The government aims to provide motorized tools to at least 50,000 artisans within the first three years of the scheme's implementation. 

The scheme targets traditional crafts that have been passed down through generations and are integral to India's cultural heritage. 

By motorizing these crafts, the government seeks to improve the quality of products and increase competitiveness in both domestic and international markets. 

The benefits of the scheme include financial assistance for purchasing motorized tools, training for artisans on how to use these tools effectively, and access to markets for selling their products. 

Artisans can receive financial assistance of up to INR 1 lakh for the purchase of motorized equipment. 

The scheme also provides for a subsidy of 50% on the cost of the motorized tools. 

This means that artisans only need to invest INR 50,000 out of pocket for tools that cost INR 1 lakh. 

Eligibility for the scheme is primarily focused on traditional artisans who have been engaged in craft production for at least three years. 

Applicants must be at least 18 years old and should have a valid identification proof such as an Aadhar card. 

Income criteria stipulate that the annual income of the artisan should not exceed INR 3 lakh. 

Artisans must also be members of a registered artisan cooperative or self-help group to qualify for the scheme. 

The application process involves several steps. 

First, interested artisans must fill out an application form available at local government offices or online through the official government portal. 

The application form requires details such as the artisan's name, address, craft type, and income details. 

Applicants must also submit proof of their craft work, which can include photographs of their products or a portfolio. 

Additionally, a recommendation letter from the local artisan cooperative or self-help group is required. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the district-level committee responsible for the scheme. 

The committee will verify the details provided and may conduct a field visit to assess the artisan's work. 

If approved, the artisan will receive a sanction letter detailing the financial assistance and the tools they are eligible for. 

The disbursement of funds is typically done through direct bank transfers to the artisan's bank account. 

The entire process from application to disbursement can take approximately 30 to 45 days, depending on the efficiency of the local administration. 

The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Textiles in collaboration with various state governments. 

State Handicrafts Development Corporations play a crucial role in facilitating the scheme at the local level. 

Artisans can contact their respective state handicrafts department for more information and assistance regarding the application process. 

The government has set a timeline for the scheme to ensure that the targeted number of artisans is reached within the stipulated period. 

Regular monitoring and evaluation will be conducted to assess the impact of the scheme on the livelihoods of artisans. 

The government aims to create a sustainable ecosystem for traditional crafts through this initiative. 

By motorizing traditional crafts, the scheme also aims to reduce the physical strain on artisans, particularly women, who often engage in labor-intensive craft production. 

The introduction of motorized tools is expected to enhance the precision and quality of craft products. 

This, in turn, will help artisans command better prices for their products in the market. 

The scheme also aligns with the government's broader goals of promoting Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat. 

By empowering artisans, the scheme contributes to the overall economic development of rural areas. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 200 crore for the initial phase of the scheme. 

This funding will support the purchase of motorized tools and provide training programs for artisans. 

Training will be conducted in collaboration with technical institutes and local NGOs to ensure that artisans are well-equipped to use the new tools. 

The government is also exploring partnerships with private sector companies to provide artisans with access to modern technology and design innovations. 

The Motorisation of Traditional Crafts scheme is expected to create job opportunities in the craft sector. 

It aims to attract younger generations to traditional crafts by making them more appealing through modernization. 

The scheme is part of the government's commitment to preserving India's rich cultural heritage while promoting economic growth. 

Artisans who benefit from the scheme will also have the opportunity to participate in national and international trade fairs. 

This exposure will help them network with potential buyers and expand their market reach. 

The government encourages artisans to form cooperatives to enhance their bargaining power and access to resources. 

The Motorisation of Traditional Crafts scheme is a significant step towards empowering artisans and ensuring the sustainability of traditional crafts in India. 

Through this initiative, the government aims to create a vibrant and thriving ecosystem for traditional artisans. 

The scheme is expected to have a lasting impact on the livelihoods of artisans and the preservation of traditional crafts in India. 

Overall, the Motorisation of Traditional Crafts scheme represents a forward-thinking approach to integrating modern technology with traditional practices. 

By providing financial assistance and training, the government is helping artisans adapt to changing market demands while preserving their cultural heritage. 

This scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to supporting the artisan community and promoting sustainable development. 

The Motorisation of Traditional Crafts scheme is a crucial initiative that highlights the importance of traditional crafts in India's economy and cultural identity. 

Artisans are encouraged to take advantage of this scheme to enhance their productivity and improve their livelihoods. 

The government is dedicated to ensuring that traditional crafts continue to thrive in the modern economy. 

Through this scheme, the government aims to create a future where traditional artisans are empowered and their crafts are celebrated.
